title: The Practice of Giving Advance Notice for Workforce Reductions
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece questions the common corporate practice of announcing workforce reductions to the media or investors before informing the affected team members directly. It acknowledges the legal and market pressures publicly traded companies face to reassure stakeholders quickly, but argues that leaders who prioritize stock price optics over internal transparency trade short-term market comfort for long-term erosion of trust. The article frames the decision as a values question, asserting that good leaders put people ahead of short-term stakeholder messaging even under pressure to do otherwise.
points: The piece criticizes announcing layoffs to media/investors before informing affected employees.
Publicly traded companies face real pressure to reassure markets quickly about cost-cutting moves.
The tradeoff is framed as short-term stock optics versus long-term erosion of employee trust.
The article treats the sequencing choice as fundamentally a values question for leaders.
quotes: As part of this cost-cutting planning process, how to communicate a reduction in headcount to both internal team members and external stakeholders is hugely consequential.
What is so confusing is why so many organizations announce RIFs through the media, sometimes even before team members learn of the impending changes.
By releasing the information to the media themselves, leaders convince themselves that they can control the narrative.
When team members are blindsided by unexpected news of reductions, they naturally feel betrayed, disrespected, and disenfranchised.
Good leaders don’t make that call because they value people more than they value short-term gain.
